title: Words taught before reading
statement: Whether a film before a reading should teach the text's words: one rule bans pre-teaching what the passage teaches, another calls the film the best place to teach a word.
detail: One version of the intro-video rules says not to pre-teach vocabulary the passage is meant to teach (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 932). The other says the video is ideally where a word gets taught, because a visual anchor, a spoken definition and later recurrence are worth considerably more than a definition on a card (line 301). The built Grade 3 lesson designs do some of both: a film stamps a few words, those are kept out of the lesson's vocabulary slot, and the lesson's taught word is a different one (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.1 - Fantasy Classics - Lesson Designs/3.1 - 1. Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp, Part 1 (FICTION, FIND) — v3 (order + MCQ QA).docx`, line 13; `downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.2 - The Living World - Lesson Designs/3.2 - 5. Feathers and Scales - CONNECT - Lesson Design (v3 - prototype-aligned).docx`, line 263). So part of the disagreement is about which words a film may teach.
